limitations: Removing one job changes worker assignments and retained histories; this design cannot independently estimate the direct write-race effect versus those downstream effects.
The original control is historical, not a contemporaneous randomized arm. Matching sealed runtime and inputs narrows, but does not eliminate, scheduling variation.
Two fixed repeats cannot estimate nondeterminism frequency. Exact agreement would not prove the duplicate mechanism necessary for every original difference.
No historical A/reference unique-cause attribution, later trajectory reproduction or locomotion claim is supported.
Execution readiness remains subject to the independent execution review and fresh preflight.

Qualified runtime model/library bytes, interpreter, distributions, CPU, source lock and sealed external inputs equal the original control qualification. Recorded checks passed 51 Python contracts, three native zero-integration checks, quality and diff checks, with no qualification optimizer calls.

The design uses two fresh fixed processes, unchanged production reset/encoder, ticks 0..10 and replans 0/10. Four independent new calls derive 4*(35*49+37+700)=9808 private upper-bound steps within 16384 reservations, with zero canonical integration and no reopening of prior ledgers.

This is a useful minimal intervention on duplicate scheduling. Repeat differences surviving verified unique t34 execution would demonstrate that duplicate simultaneous writes are unnecessary for those observed differences. Warmstart seed differences alone do not establish effects on selected controls.

Exact outputs after dedup would be consistent with duplicate removal or its downstream scheduling/history effects. The task correctly avoids claiming that this outcome uniquely identifies a write race or excludes warmstart history.
The prior 8.549605468033405e-12 repeat difference is about 0.855% of the unchanged 1e-9 threshold. It is an exact-repeatability observation, not a threshold or performance failure.
